module_title: Union & Its Territory and Citizenship - Basic Understanding
introduction: Part I (Articles 1-4) of the Constitution deals with the Union and its Territory, defining India's geographical boundaries and how new states can be formed. Part II (Articles 5-11) deals with Citizenship, defining who belongs to the Indian nation. India follows the principle of 'Single Citizenship'.

core_concepts.title: Article 1: Name and Territory of the Union
core_concepts.description: Article 1 describes India, that is, 'Bharat', as a 'Union of States' rather than a 'Federation of States'. This means states have no right to secede from the Union.

core_concepts.title: Formation of New States (Article 3)
core_concepts.description: Parliament has the power to form a new state, increase or decrease the area of any state, and alter the boundaries or name of any existing state by passing a simple law.

core_concepts.title: Single Citizenship
core_concepts.description: Unlike the USA, which has dual citizenship (national and state), India provides only a single national citizenship to all its people, irrespective of the state they are born or reside in.

core_concepts.title: Acquisition of Citizenship
core_concepts.description: Under the Citizenship Act of 1955, there are 5 ways to acquire Indian citizenship: by Birth, by Descent, by Registration, by Naturalization, and by Incorporation of territory.

important_entities.name: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
important_entities.significance: He clarified that the term 'Union' was deliberately used to indicate that the Indian federation is not the result of an agreement among the states, making the union indestructible.

important_entities.name: Parliament of India
important_entities.significance: Under Article 11, Parliament has the absolute power to make laws regarding the acquisition and termination of citizenship.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Union of India vs. Territory of India
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: These are not the same! 'Union of India' includes ONLY the states. 'Territory of India' is a wider concept that includes States, Union Territories (UTs), and any territories that may be acquired by India in the future.

India is called an 'Indestructible Union of Destructible States' because the Centre can change the name/boundaries of a state without its consent. The USA, conversely, is an 'Indestructible Union of Indestructible States'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Birth, Registration, Acquisition (of territory), Naturalization, Descent.

exam_strategy_tips: Always remember that Part I covers Articles 1 to 4, and Part II covers Articles 5 to 11.
Questions often ask who holds the power to alter state boundaries or regulate citizenship. The answer is ALWAYS the 'Parliament' (not the President or State Legislature).
